H1521.d: Gichon, a river of Paradise; also a valley (or pool) near Jerusalem
fb: Two waters carry the name. One is a river out of Eden that circles Cush and has never been matched to a known river. The other is Jerusalem's only natural spring, in the Kidron Valley, which Hezekiah ran underground into the city before Sennacherib's siege, and the tunnel can still be walked.

H1571.d: properly, assemblage; used only adverbially also, even, yea, though; often repeated as correl. both...and

H1512.d: the external abdomen, belly (as the source of the faetus)

H1540.d: to denude (especially in a disgraceful sense); by implication, to exile (captives being usually stripped); figuratively, to reveal

H1586.d: Gomer, the name of a son of Japheth and of his descendants; also of a Hebrewess
fb: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
Genesis 10 makes him a son of Japheth, and the name stands for his descendants too, which is how Ezekiel 38:6 can list Gomer as a nation. Hosea's wife has the same name and is a different person.
Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Hosea names her once, and she is a woman from the divided-kingdom years.

H1558.d: a circumstance (as rolled around); only used adverbially, on account of

H1580.d: to treat a person (well or ill), i.e. benefit or requite; by implication (of toil), to ripen, i.e. (specifically) to wean

fb: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
One of the sons Nahor, Abraham's brother, had by his concubine Reumah. Nothing further is recorded.

H1589.d: to thieve (literally or figuratively); by implication, to deceive

H1568.d: Gilad, a region East of the Jordan; also the name of three Israelites
fb: Hill country east of the Jordan, split by the Jabbok between Og in the north and Sihon in the south before the conquest. Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh got it, and its rough ground made it a refuge for Jacob running from Laban and David running from Absalom. Jeremiah's question about balm in Gilead comes from its trade in balm and spices.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
The man, not the region. Numbers 26 and Joshua 17 put him in Manasseh's family, and Chronicles lists him there again.
One of 4 men called Gilead. This one is a man from the years before the monarchy, named twice in Judges.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 1 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

H1530.d: something rolled, i.e. a heap of stone or dung (plural ruins), by analogy, a spring of water (plural waves)

H1567.d: Galed, a memorial cairn East of the Jordan
fb: Not a person but a heap of stones. Jacob and Laban piled it up to seal their covenant. Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha in Aramaic, and Jacob's Hebrew name for it means heap of witness.

H1517.d: a thong (as compressing); by analogy, a tendon

H1548.d: properly, to be bald, i.e. (causatively) to shave; figuratively to lay waste

H1573.d: properly, an absorbent, i.e. the bulrush (from its porosity); specifically the papyrus

H1538.d: a skull (as round); by implication, a head (in enumeration of persons)

H1544.d: properly, a log (as round); by implication, an idol

fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
He turns up five times in Numbers, always in the wilderness lists of tribal leaders, and he is not the Pharisee who taught Paul.
Man living at the time of the New Testament
Acts names him twice, and he is a man from the New Testament.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Ammiel's father, and Ammiel was Dan's spy; Numbers 13:12 is the only place Gemalli appears.

H1516.d: a gorge (from its lofty sides; hence, narrow, but not a gully or winter-torrent)

H1569.d: a Giladite or descendant of Gilad
fb: Someone from Gilead, east of the Jordan, or of the clan named after Machir's son. Jephthah is the best known, the judge who beat the Ammonites and made the rash vow about his daughter.

H1537.d: Gilgal, the name of three places in Palestine
fb: Israel's first camp after crossing the Jordan. The people were circumcised there and kept their first Passover in the land, and later Samuel judged at Gilgal and Saul was confirmed as king there.
Named once, in 2 Kings, and nowhere else.

The same city as Gezer. Pharaoh took it and gave it to his daughter when she married Solomon, and Solomon fortified it along with Hazor and Megiddo. The Gezer Calendar, a little tablet of farming seasons in early Hebrew script, was found there.

H1543.d: a fountain, bowl or globe (all as round)

fb: Ahithophel came from Giloh, in Judah's hill country southwest of Hebron. When Absalom took Hushai's advice over his, he went home to Giloh and hanged himself.
On Benjamin's border, near the Jordan. It is generally taken as another name for the Gilgal of Joshua 15:7, though which Gilgal is uncertain, since the name just means circles.

H1551.d: Galil (as a special circuit) in the North of Palestine
fb: Jesus grew up here and did most of his public work around the Sea of Galilee. Judeans thought the north provincial and mixed, which is the edge on Nathanael's question about whether anything good could come out of Nazareth.

H1576.d: treatment, i.e. an act (of good or ill); by implication, service or requital

H1518.d: to gush forth (as water), generally to issue

fb: Giant living at the time of United Monarchy

The Philistine champion from Gath whom the young David killed in the valley of Elah. The traditional Hebrew text makes him over nine feet, while the Dead Sea Scrolls and the earliest Greek give about six foot nine. One later passage credits Elhanan, and Chronicles makes Elhanan's man Goliath's brother.
Michal was given to Palti of Gallim after Saul took her away from David. Isaiah lists the town, in Benjamin north of Jerusalem, among the places panicking as the Assyrian army comes on.

H1511.d: a Grizite (collectively) or member of a native tribe in Palestine
fb: David raided them from Ziklag along with the Geshurites and Amalekites. Most read the name as Girzites, an otherwise unknown desert tribe in the Negev toward Egypt, and not the people of Gezer.

Saul died on these hills above the Jezreel Valley. The Philistines broke his army, three of his sons fell, Jonathan among them, and Saul, badly wounded, took his own life. David's lament curses Gilboa never to have dew or rain.
It exists in the record only to locate the hill of Ammah, where Joab gave up chasing Abner in the war between the houses of David and Saul. Its site has never been identified.

H1526.d: a Gilonite or inhabitant of Giloh
fb: It is what Ahithophel is called, since he came from Giloh. He was David's trusted counsellor, then Absalom's, and he hanged himself when his advice was turned down.

H1504.d: to cut down or off; (figuratively) to destroy, divide, exclude, or decide

H1550.d: a valve of a folding door (as turning); also a ring (as round)

fb: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
He was born to the Edomite prince Hadad and the sister of Tahpenes, Pharaoh's wife, and grew up in Pharaoh's own house with the royal children.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
He is named as Tibni's father, and for four years Tibni's supporters fought Omri for the throne of Israel until Omri won.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy

Elisha's servant. When Elisha turned down Naaman's payment, Gehazi ran after the general and lied his way into silver and clothes, and Elisha, who knew without being there, gave him Naaman's leprosy for good.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Caleb's line, through his son Jahdai, in the genealogy of Judah.

H1559.d: Galal, the name of two Israelites
fb: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
A Levite among those who settled back in Jerusalem after the exile, listed in Chronicles and Nehemiah.
Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a Levite from the exile and the return.

H1523.d: properly, to spin round (under the influence of any violent emotion), i.e. usually rejoice, or (as cringing) fear

fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
The twenty-second of the twenty-four priestly divisions David set up for the temple went by his name.
The Philistines took it and its villages in the reign of Ahaz. It was a lowland town known for sycamores, and the name survives in Jimzu, a village southeast of Lydda.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
They came back from Babylon with Zerubbabel, the descendants of Gahar, one of the families of temple servants called the Nethinim.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Temple servants, the Nethinim, who came home from Babylon with Zerubbabel, counted under his name. Nothing further is known of him.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A priest who came back from Babylon with Zerubbabel, and his family is one of the priestly houses Nehemiah lists.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
In the procession at the dedication of Nehemiah's walls he was one of the priests' sons playing instruments. Nothing further is recorded about him.

H1565.d: sterile (as wrapped up too hard); figuratively, desolate

H1524.d: a revolution (of time, i.e. an age); also joy

H1503.d: the trunk or stump of a tree (as felled or as planted)

H1584.d: to end (in the sense of completion or failure)
H1584.g: may it come to an end

H1534.d: a wheel; by analogy, a whirlwind; also dust (as whirled)

H1564.d: a wrapped (and unformed mass, i.e. as the embryo)

H1549.d: a tablet for writing (as bare); by analogy, a mirror (as a plate)

H1587.d: Gemarjah, the name of two Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A royal scribe, and Baruch read Jeremiah's scroll aloud from his chamber; later his son tried and failed to stop King Jehoiakim burning it.
Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Jeremiah names him once, and he is a priest from the divided-kingdom years.

H1508.d: the figure or person (as if cut out); also an inclosure (as separated)

fb: Soldiers in the towers of Tyre, beside the men of Arvad, in Ezekiel's oracle. Who they were is debated: a place called Gammad, or just a word for brave warriors.
